newsitem.title: USA: Starr seeks longer term for Whitewater grand jury.
newsitem.headline: Starr seeks longer term for Whitewater grand jury.

text.p: Whitewater special prosecutor Kenneth Starr on Tuesday sought an extension of the Whitewater investigation into the political and private business affairs of President Bill Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton.
In a motion filed in U.S. District Court at Little Rock, Starr said a grand jury had gathered substantial evidence of obstruction of justice and needed more time to pursue its probe.
The special prosecutor asked a federal judge to extend the life of the grand jury, which was scheduled to be dismissed May 7, through early November.
"This grand jury has heard extensive evidence of possible obstruction of justice relating to matters within the Independent Counsel's jurisdiction," Starr wrote.
"Moreover," Starr said, "the information provided to the grand jury by Jim McDougal emphasises the continued need to obtain the testimony of Susan McDougal."
In the late 1970s Jim and Susan McDougal, with President and Mrs. Clinton, were the original investors in a failed Arkansas real estate project called Whitewater.

The McDougals, who divorced several years ago, were convicted in 1996 of fraud and conspiracy in a trial in which a government witness testified that he loaned Susan McDougal money that was diverted to the Whitewater project. The witness, businessman David Hale, also testified that Clinton, then governor of Arkansas, pressured him to make the loan.
Clinton denied the allegation in videotaped testimony played for the jury.

Jim McDougal began assisting Starr's investigation last August and was given a sharply reduced sentence -- three years in prison and three years probation -- last week after prosecutors praised his cooperation.

At his trial last year, McDougal disputed government testimony that Clinton was present at a meeting in which the loan to Susan McDougal was discussed. But in recent days McDougal has recanted and said Clinton was a participant.

Susan McDougal has been jailed since last September for refusing to answer questions before the grand jury. One of the questions she said she refused to answer was whether Clinton testified truthfully.
"The grand jury cannot complete its consideration of the informtion and testimony of Jim McDougal before its presently scheduled expiration date," Starr said on Tuesday.
The grand jury was to have been dismissed on May 7.
White House chief of staff Erskine Bowles and presidential counsellor Thomas "Mack" McLarty testified before the grand jury last week.

Expected to appear soon are Bruce Lindsay, Clinton's deputy White House counsel, and Truman Arnold, a Texas oil man who has been a principal contributor to Clinton and the Democratic National Committee.
